name: facet_demo
description: DEMO fixture for the R2 facet ladder — NOT the benchmark fixture. Small, hand-authored corpus that exercises every mechanism (stale distractor, wrong-repo distractor, symbol rename, paraphrase pair, a vague query where embedding should win). The real 50-memory / 20-query gold fixture is a pair-authoring task with ctharvey (R2 plan Risk #1: 'fixture too clean'); this only proves the pieces run end-to-end.

memories.text: Fixed the menhir recall floor so BM25-found candidates are no longer cut by the cosine similarity threshold. The source-aware floor now gates only VECTOR candidates in recall_service.py. As of 2026-06-20 this is the current behavior.

Previously the menhir recall floor in recall_service.py applied a single cosine similarity threshold to every candidate, which cut BM25 matches. This was the old approach before the source-aware floor.
archolith-bench applies a score floor to filter weak candidates before scoring in the benchmark harness. Unrelated to menhir recall, but also talks about a floor and candidates.
Added weighted_rrf in hybrid_retrieval.py to blend the vector and BM25 passes on rank instead of raw score, avoiding the BM25/cosine scale mismatch.
Renamed the graphiti search entry point: search_scored is now exposed alongside search_ranked_by_method for per-method ranked passes in graphiti_client.py.
The menhir ingest pipeline stamps each episode with a request id and namespace during enrichment.
archolith-bench BM25 baseline uses Okapi BM25 with k1=1.5 and b=0.75 over scenario text for the retrieval ladder.
The menhir scoring_service floor is now source-aware: it gates only VECTOR candidates and exempts BM25, pending, and file-linked sources in scoring_service.py.
Honestly the whole recall experience felt sluggish and frustrating today, like it was grinding through too much before returning anything useful.
Note: the menhir belief layer used to keep stale assertions in the same bucket as current ones, which leaked historical context into current-truth queries.
